Presenter script

I could not complete ten live interviews. Instead, I built an online survey app in three languages, with separate questions for riders and drivers.

After removing one duplicate, I had sixty-two responses. Fifty-eight were riders and four were drivers. Thirty people wrote answers, and eleven shared detailed experiences. The survey gave useful signals, but no live follow-up. So, it does not replace interviews.

text:
Presenter script

My goal was to understand what goes wrong during a difficult pickup and how people solve it today.

The problem statement is simple. At complex locations, the map pin may show the right area, but the rider and driver still lack one clear meeting place. This causes calls, waiting, movement, and delay.

The rider is the main user, and the driver is also affected. Success means fewer calls and a faster trip start after the driver arrives.

Sources:
Local evidence: synthesis/01-survey-insights.md, synthesis/02-strategy-implications.md, and v2/requirement.md.

The problem affected many people in the sample, but not everyone. Twenty-four out of fifty-one recent Uber car users reported difficulty or uncertainty.

Among twenty-eight problem cases, twenty-three had faced the problem before. Twenty said calling or messaging helped, while six said nothing helped. These numbers describe this sample only. They do not represent all Hyderabad users.

text:
Presenter script

The direction is simple. Help the rider and driver agree on a clear meeting place when pickup becomes difficult.

First, test a structured meeting note. Next, test help for a stuck pickup. Finally, test guidance for selected venues. This is a test order, not a final roadmap.

Presenter script

The first test is a short note before the driver arrives. At a complex location, the rider can share the gate, landmark, road side, or waiting spot.

We should test whether this reduces calls, waiting, pickup-point changes, and cancellations. It should appear only where useful, so normal pickups stay quick.

Presenter script

My recommendation is to test the structured meeting note first. It is the smallest idea that directly addresses the problem we observed.

The research has gaps. I did not complete live interviews, only four drivers responded, and the sample does not represent Hyderabad. Next, we should interview riders and drivers, then test at a few complex locations using actual pickup-delay data.

The appendix and evidence ZIP contain the supporting material. Thank you.
